1: Hi, I'm Maxwell. This is Continuity.
The glass is full in one shot, empty in the next. Someone was supposed to catch it.
2: Film is shot out of order, over weeks.
Someone has to remember how the world looked last time. The wound on the left cheek. The ring worn only after the wedding.
They're good at it. They still miss things.
3: Two continuity problems, one word for both.
Shot continuity: two shots that look alike. Line them up, diff the pixels. Solved in 2009.
Story continuity is the open one. Left cheek in April, right cheek in June. The shots look nothing alike.
Every tool works on pixels. The errors that reach the cinema are the ones that don't.
4: So stop comparing images. Compare claims about the world.
For every shot and every line, extract what's true. Who's there, what they wear, what's injured and where.
Two shots that share no pixels can still contradict each other.
5: Two sources of claims: what a shot shows, and what a line says.
They land in one ClickHouse table. A query finds the pairs that can't both be true.
Then Gemini judges: explained, or an error?
The database never judges. The model never scans.
6: This is the deployed product. Gemini over the ClickHouse MCP server, live.
Every finding shows both frames, and whether the old tools could reach it.
7: We ran the old pixel method on the errors we found. It couldn't line up the frames ninety-two percent of the time.
So that ninety-two percent is what the old tools miss, and we catch.
8: Some contradictions have no second frame at all.
The driver's scratches: right hand at seventeen minutes, wrist at thirty-nine.
Same injury, two ways, no pixels to compare. Only this finds it.
9: And we try to kill our own findings first.
Five hundred candidates. The judge flags ten. Then a second model, built to refute them, attacks each.
One survives: a bruise that switched sides of a forehead.
A watch that seems to move wrists gets refuted. A wound that moves does not.
10: And it's not one film. It's three.
A 1945 quota-quickie lights up. Night of the Living Dead gives real errors.
But a careful 2015 animated film comes back clean. Zero false errors.
It flags in proportion to how error-prone the film is. No human judged that.
11: We compare claims about the world.
